import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Ben Green's Open Problem 62

Let $p$ be a large prime, and let $A$ be the set of all primes less than $p$.
Is every $x \in \{1, \ldots, p-1\}$ congruent to some product $a_1 a_2$ where $a_1, a_2 \in A$?

This is a problem of Erdős, Odlyzko, and Sárközy [105] from 1987.

*Reference:* [Ben Green's Open Problem 62](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.62)
-/
open Filter
namespace Green62

/--
Let $p$ be a large prime, and let $A$ be the set of all primes less than $p$.
Is every $x \in \{1, \ldots, p-1\}$ congruent to some product $a_1 a_2$ where $a_1, a_2 \in A$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem green_62 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ᶠ p in atTop, p.Prime →
        let A := (Finset.range p).filter Nat.Prime
        ∀ x : ℕ, 1 ≤ x ∧ x < p →
          ∃ a₁ ∈ A, ∃ a₂ ∈ A, (x : ZMod p) = (a₁ * a₂ : ZMod p) := by
  sorry

end Green62

findings.description: The module docstring at line 25 cites Erdős, Odlyzko, and Sárközy as “[105]”, but that number identifies an unrelated paper in the currently linked Green PDF. The authors, year, and mathematical statement are correct; only the numerical reference is stale.
findings.source_evidence: https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf, Problem 62, p. 30, attributes the problem to “Erdős, Odlyzko and Sárközy [113] from 1987”. On p. 53, [113] is On the residues of products of prime numbers, whereas [105] is Erdélyi's paper on unimodular zeros of self-reciprocal polynomials.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the bare “[105]” with a named bibliographic reference to Erdős, Odlyzko, and Sárközy, On the residues of products of prime numbers, Period. Math. Hungar. 18 (1987), 229–239, preferably linking https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1987-22.pdf. The numerical reference in the current Green PDF is [113].

reformulations.difference: Lean expresses “a large prime” using eventual quantification over all natural numbers with a primality guard, and congruence using equality in ZMod. It uses representatives 1 ≤ x < p and factors strictly below p; the recent primary paper instead speaks of reduced residue classes and allows prime factors ≤ p.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Filter.eventually_atTop expands to an existential threshold N followed by all p ≥ N; the primality implication restricts precisely to prime moduli. Finset membership expands to a < p ∧ a.Prime. Multiplicativity of natural casts and ZMod.natCast_eq_natCast_iff identify the displayed equality with x ≡ a₁a₂ (mod p). For prime p, the representatives 1,…,p−1 give exactly the nonzero, hence reduced, residue classes. A product representing a nonzero class cannot have either factor equal to p, so allowing factors ≤ p is equivalent to requiring factors < p. These threshold/congruence and nonzero-residue formulations were proved equivalent in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without using the admitted problem theorem.

review.notes: No mathematical misformalization was found in the sole theorem. The answer placeholder has the correct yes/no type and scope, and both existential memberships impose conjunctions. Boundary checks confirm that p = 0 and p = 1 are excluded by primality; small-prime failures do not contradict the sufficiently-large formulation. Lean checks established arbitrarily large admissible prime moduli, tested small prime sets and representation failures, and verified the finite representation property for p = 211 using native_decide. The current Green PDF reports progress only to three factors, and Matomäki–Teräväinen explicitly say the two-factor conjecture remains open even under GRH; the recorded research-open status agrees.
